items.title: Anwar surprises diplomats with Bollywood performance [WATCH]
items.summary: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim surprised diplomats during his official visit to India for the BRICS Summit by singing a classic Bollywood song. Anwar, in India for the BRICS Summit, was seen singing the classic Hindi song at a hotel in New Delhi, accompanied by a pianist and with both hands raised in the air. The performance reflected Anwar's long-standing appreciation of Hindi cinema and music, including during his engagements with India, an important economic partner.

items.title: Indian woman drowns after falling from boat during Tioman diving trip
items.summary: KUANTAN, Sept 13 — An Indian national drowned after she was believed to have slipped off a boat following a scuba diving activity in the waters of Renggis, Pulau Tioman in Rompin yesterday. Rompin district police chief Supt Sharif Shai Sharif Mondoi said police received a call from the Tekek Health Clinic at about 10 am regarding the drowning of Sabiya Shiek, 65. He said initial investigations revealed the victim had taken part in a discovery scuba diving session with six family members, accompanied by two instructors and a dive master.

items.title: Thai man drowns in Sungai Golok near Malaysia-Thailand border
items.summary: OTA BHARU, Sept 13 — A 23-year-old Thai man was found drowned in Sungai Golok along the Malaysia-Thailand border near Kampung Pengkalan Pasir and Abe Yie in Rantau Panjang, Pasir Mas yesterday evening. Rantau Panjang Fire and Rescue Station chief Hamzah Musa said the victim, Faiz Hasan, was found by Thai authorities at 7.10 pm while a search and rescue operation was underway. Hamzah said the victim’s body was taken by Thai authorities for further action, while the search and rescue operation was fully called off at 7.15 pm today.

items.title: Anwar says Malaysia set to gain from new investment, industrial cooperation with India
items.summary: NEW DELHI, Sept 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said his meetings with representatives of several leading companies here today reflect the continued confidence of industry players and investors in Malaysia’s economic potential and direction. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, met representatives of DRB-Hicom, Segula Technologies India, AWL Agri Business Ltd and Motherson Group to discuss opportunities to expand investment and industrial cooperation between Malaysia and India in strategic sectors. “I also met with representatives of Motherson Group, who shared plans to expand their information technology and digital solutions business in Malaysia,” the Prime Minister said.

items.title: Anwar to outline Malaysia’s vision for inclusive global growth at Brics summit
items.summary: NEW DELHI, Sept 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is scheduled to deliver a National Statement on Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth at the 18th Brics Leaders’ Summit here today. Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, was accompanied by Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri Ramanan Ramakrishnan. As part of the visit, the Prime Minister is scheduled to meet Chief Minister Thiru V. D. Satheesan and Governor of Keralam Thiru Rajendra Vishwanath Arleka.

items.title: One dead, 30 missing after ferry sinks off Vanuatu
items.summary: SYDNEY: One person died and 30 are missing after a ferry sank off the coast of Vanuatu, the South Pacific nation's government said on Sunday. "Over 30 people remain missing at sea," it said. The centre said 12 people were located on Sunday morning.

items.title: Houthis claim Saudi base strike as Yemen fighting displaces 76,000
items.summary: SANAA: Houthi fighters on Sunday said they used drones and missiles to attack a military base in southern Saudi Arabia as renewed fighting with Yemen's government forces forced growing numbers of civilians to flee. Clashes have increased this week between the Iran-allied Houthis and Yemeni government forces, which are backed by Riyadh. On Saturday, the government forces said they had struck Houthi fighters in the Red Sea city of Mocha, and later attacked other Houthi positions in the southwestern part of the country.

items.title: City folk: Keep walkways clear
items.summary: They said converting pedestrian footpaths into dining areas compromises public safety, obstructs vulnerable groups and prioritises local council revenue over urban mobility. Hotelier Nizam Hamid, 42, from Jalan Klang Lama, said forcing pedestrians off designated walkways and onto busy roads presents a safety hazard. Nizam said walkways have historically served as sheltered pedestrian corridors, providing safe passage alongside shoplots.

items.title: Walkway dining welcomed, but safety comes first, say operators
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Restaurant operators have welcomed Kuala Lumpur City Hall's (DBKL) decision to allow eateries to place tables and chairs on five-foot walkways, but emphasised that member restaurants will strictly prioritise customer safety. Malaysian Indian Restaurant Owners Association president Datuk J. Govindasamy said while operators are eager to start expanding, safety cannot be compromised. Safety must come first."

items.title: DBKL: Walkway dining policy in place since 2017, subject to conditions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Allowing eatery operators to place tables and chairs on walkways is not a new policy, but an enhancement of guidelines established in 2017, said Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL). Responding to queries about public safety concerns and regulatory enforcement, a DBKL spokesman said ongoing improvements to the framework aimed to ensure clearer, standardised implementation aligned with current needs. "DBKL has not introduced any new policy allowing outdoor tables and chairs.

items.title: [FULL TEXT] Sultan Nazrin's royal address at the 17th SC-OCIS Roundtable
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The following is the royal address by the Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah, titled "Building Resilience: The Intersection Between Capital, Climate and Innovation". It was delivered at the 17th SC-OCIS Roundtable, held at the Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies in the United Kingdom. The beautiful structure around us stands as testament to that vision - a physical tribute to the joining of these two great traditions.

items.title: Pedestrian walkways no place for chairs and tables [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A coalition of residents' associations is gravely disappointed with the government and Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) over the decision to allow restaurant operators to place tables and chairs on public walkways. Save Kuala Lumpur (SKL) chairman Datuk M. Ali expressed deep frustration over the lack of public consultation and questioned why authorities are prioritising business operators over the safety and interests of residents. This followed recent engagements between Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh, Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud, the Selangor and Kuala Lumpur Chinese Coffee Shop and Tea Shop Owners' Association, and the Malaysia Muslim Restaurant Operators Association.

items.title: China, Russia, Iran leaders gather in India as BRICS nations seek common ground
items.summary: NEW DELHI: Chinese President Xi Jinping joined the leaders of Russia, Iran, India and other BRICS nations in New Delhi on Saturday, seeking common ground on the Middle East war as deep divisions test the 11-member bloc. Xi told the summit that the Middle East war "does not serve the common interests of the international community", according to Chinese state news agency Xinhua. "We have to transform this pyramid of privilege into a platform of partnership," Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi told Xi, Russian President Vladimir Putin, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and other leaders.

items.title: Asean needs stronger political will, accountability to tackle haze
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution needs stronger political commitment, faster regional responses and greater accountability if the region is to break the cycle of recurring haze, experts said. He said Asean ministers should review the mechanism given the impact of transboundary haze on public health. Tunku Mohar said Asean's consensus-based decision-making could make reforms difficult.

items.title: From dishwasher in Melbourne to heading the kitchen at Gilda in George Town, a Malaysian (food) love story
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 13 — Before he was brining chicken and making coconut milk-laced romesco at Gilda Restaurant, Ahmad Soffian Salim was washing plates in restaurants more than 14 years ago. Chef Ahmad working in the open kitchen. ”I love food but what really made me want to be a chef was the high quality local produce there,” Ahmad said.

items.title: Temiar facial art tradition embraces a modern touch while preserving its heritage
items.summary: Endah Angah, 37, said the practice of painting geometric motifs, including long and wavy lines and dots, on the face remained deeply cherished by her community as an enduring symbol of its cultural heritage. “Using modern cosmetics is much easier for us. Rahimah Punai, 39, said modern cosmetics might have changed the way the facial motifs were created, but their spiritual meaning and connection to their ancestral heritage remained intact.

items.title: BRICS nations call for 'maximum restraint' in Middle East war
items.summary: NEW DELHI: Members of the 11-nation BRICS group including China, Russia, Iran and India called for calm in the Middle East at a summit in New Delhi on Saturday, overcoming earlier divisions to issue a joint statement. Chinese President Xi Jinping, who joined Russian, Iranian, Indian and other leaders in India's capital, told the summit that the Middle East war "does not serve the common interests of the international community." But leaders issued a statement on Saturday after intense diplomatic efforts by host India, as the bloc seeks to bolster its global influence and address conflict, trade turbulence and energy security.

items.title: Modi, Xi push business links, border peace as India-China ties revive
items.summary: NEW DELHI: India and China's leaders pledged on Saturday to build up business and transport links, New Delhi said, as both rebuild ties badly damaged by a 2020 military clash on their disputed Himalayan border. Bilateral trade reached a record US$155.6 billion in 2025, according to Chinese customs data. India's exports to China remain much smaller, leaving New Delhi with a trade deficit of more than US$100 billion.

items.title: Trump backs Irish unification, calls it 'a fantastic thing'
items.summary: DOONBEG, Ireland: Donald Trump said Saturday he would "love to see" a united Ireland, wading into a politically sensitive subject as he embarked on a two-day Irish visit that blurs the lines between his presidency and personal business interests. After meeting Ireland's Prime Minister Micheal Martin in Dublin, Trump said reunification of the Republic of Ireland and Northern Ireland – split for over a century – would be "a fantastic thing." The island of Ireland has been split between the Irish republic in the south and Northern Ireland, which is part of the United Kingdom, since 1921.

items.title: #NSTviral: DBKL urged to act on double-parking gridlock along Jalan Pudu Lama
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) has been urged to take action against illegal parking along Jalan Pudu Lama, where double-parking has reportedly reduced the two-way road to a single congested lane. The issue was highlighted in a viral post on Threads by user @zebra.animal.53, who tagged DBKL's parking enforcement account and questioned the lack of action over vehicles parked on both sides of the road. From Bursa Malaysia to Jalan Pudu Lama, cars are parked on both sides of the road even though it is a two-way street," the user posted after tagging DBKL parking on Threads.

items.title: Former judge Syed Ahmad Idid denies requesting RM10.5mil compensation over 1996 resignation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former High Court judge Datuk Syed Ahmad Idid Syed Abdullah Idid has clarified that he never requested, demanded, or set a compensation amount of RM10.5 million from the Malaysian government over his resignation nearly 30 years ago. He clarified to clear up confusion regarding the reported claim through a letter sent today to Malaysian Bar president Anand Raj. Syed Ahmad Idid also expressed his deep appreciation to the Malaysian Bar for its firm stance in defending the independence and integrity of the judiciary through its statement issued yesterday, titled "The Judiciary Must Be, and Remain, Steadfast in Upholding the Rule of Law and Incorruptible".

items.title: BRICS calls for immediate restoration of WTO dispute settlement mechanism
items.summary: NEW DELHI: BRICS has called for the immediate restoration of an accessible, effective, and fully functioning two-tier binding World Trade Organisation (WTO) dispute settlement mechanism while reaffirming its support for a rules-based multilateral trading system. BRICS said it would enhance coordination under its Informal Consultative Framework to address challenges undermining the WTO's effectiveness and credibility. "We strongly advocate for the immediate restoration of an accessible, effective, fully functioning, two-tier binding WTO dispute settlement mechanism as a foundation for trust and predictability for all WTO members, and the appointment of new Appellate Body members without further delay," the declaration stated.

items.title: Dr L. Sivanaesan appointed new MMA president
items.summary: IPOH: Dr L Sivanaesan has been appointed the new president of the Malaysian Medical Association (MMA), succeeding Datuk Dr R Thirunavukarasu, whose term ended today. The former MMA president-elect previously served as chairman of MMA Selangor, honorary deputy secretary of the association for two terms, and chairman of the MMA Private Practitioners Section from 2023 to 2024. Speaking at the MMA 2026 dinner here tonight, Sivanaesan said retaining doctors in Malaysia's public healthcare system will be his priority as the nation faces growing healthcare demands and an increasing need for medical personnel.

items.title: Man arrested over robbery and assault of two Rohingya men
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Police have arrested a 25-year-old local man suspected of robbing, assaulting, and threatening two Rohingya men in Taman Perling. Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said police received reports regarding the incidents on Sept 9 and 10 from the victims, aged 25 and 35. Ab Rahaman said police seized a lawnmower, a parang, a UNHCR card, a motorcycle key, and a set of clothes.

items.title: Johari, Piyush Goyal discuss stronger Malaysia-India economic ties
items.summary: NEW DELHI: Investment, trade and economic cooperation between Malaysia and India were the focus of a bilateral meeting between Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and India's Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal during Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's visit to New Delhi. Johari said the productive and constructive discussion focused on concrete measures to strengthen trade, investment and economic cooperation between Malaysia and India. Anwar is in India from Sept 11 to 15 for engagements in New Delhi and Keralam.

items.title: Could AI really kill us all?
items.summary: AI experts have long described the threat as critical. Such existential fears do not concern current AI systems, he said. "We are less intelligent than superintelligent AI.

items.title: The morning that changed everything
items.summary: The next year, he was appointed news editor of the university's newspaper due in large part to his experience, meagre as it was. One fateful morning that year, the journalist in question woke up a little late and rushed to get ready, forgoing his usual habit of watching the news on TV. The journalist thought nothing of it, thinking it was a light aircraft.

items.title: NST Leader: Greater Sabah, Sarawak representation a step towards equity
items.summary: THIS marks a positive and long-awaited step towards addressing the imbalance in Malaysia's federal structure and fulfilling the broader spirit of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63). Greater representation for Sabah and Sarawak is a positive recognition that Malaysia's federal structure must evolve to reflect the realities and aspirations of all its regions. Greater representation would recognise the special position of Sabah and Sarawak as partners in the formation of Malaysia.

items.title: Sarawak extends school closures in Serian, Lubok Antu over haze
items.summary: KUCHING: The state education department has extended the temporary closure of schools in the Serian and Lubok Antu districts until the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading drops below 200. The Sarawak State Education Department said the decision followed continuous monitoring of API readings via the Department of Environment's Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) and reports from the Malaysian Meteorological Department. The department added that the Education Ministry, in collaboration with the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), will soon distribute face masks to students, teachers, and staff at schools in severely affected areas.

items.title: Sanusi, Mahdzir set to meet over possible Pas-Umno cooperation
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI: A meeting between Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor and state Umno leaders is being arranged to discuss possible cooperation between the two parties. Sanusi, who is also Kedah Pas deputy commissioner, said he had been informed about the proposed meeting and his office was arranging a suitable date. "I have also obtained Kedah Pas' approval to hold an initial meeting with former Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Mahdzir Khalid from Umno.

items.title: Putin conveys warm regards to Sultan Ibrahim, praises strong Malaysia-Russia relations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Russian President Vladimir Putin conveyed his warm regards to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, during a bilateral meeting with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim yesterday. Earlier, Bernama reported that Anwar conveyed warm regards from Sultan Ibrahim to the Russian president and reiterated His Majesty's invitation to Putin to undertake a state visit to Malaysia. Sultan Ibrahim, who ascended the federal throne on Jan 31, 2024, has visited Russia three times: a state visit in August 2025, a special visit in January 2026, and a visit to Moscow in May for Russia's Victory Day celebrations.

items.title: SC proposes sukuk framework for climate resilience
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Securities Commission (SC) has proposed a new purpose-driven sukuk framework aimed at mobilising capital for climate adaptation, resilience and sustainable development, as the country faces growing exposure to climate-related risks. SC chairman Datuk Mohammad Faiz Azmi said the proposed framework, to be known as Sukuk Prisma SDG, would build on Malaysia's existing Sustainable and Responsible Investment (SRI) sukuk framework. Mohammad Faiz said Malaysia, located in a climate-vulnerable region, had suffered more than US$2.2 billion (RM8.95 billion) in losses from floods — its main climate risk — over the past five years.

items.title: Take control of what we put into our lungs
items.summary: Behind Air Pollutant Index (API) numbers are real people, including children going to school, workers commuting to the office, elderly people going about daily routines and individuals with respiratory and cardiovascular problems trying to breathe normally. This is why people are repeatedly advised to reduce outdoor activities when air quality deteriorates. Why expose our lungs to cigarette smoke when the air around us is already polluted?

items.title: Anwar looks forward to meeting India's Grand Mufti during Keralam visit
items.summary: KERALAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is looking forward to meeting India's Grand Mufti Sheikh Abubakr Ahmad during his visit to Keralam tomorrow, following his participation in the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit. Responding to a message from Sheikh Abubakr Ahmad welcoming him and the Malaysian delegation to India, Anwar expressed his gratitude to the Grand Mufti. Sheikh Abubakr Ahmad had earlier expressed particular appreciation for Anwar's decision to include Jamia Markaz, one of India's premier Islamic institutions, in his itinerary.

items.title: Calicut in focus ahead of Anwar's visit to Keralam after BRICS Summit
items.summary: KERALAM: The historic city of Calicut, also known as Kozhikode, in Keralam is drawing international attention ahead of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's visit tomorrow, following his participation in the 18th BRICS Summit. A check around Calicut today showed the city bustling with daily activities as interest in the prime minister's arrival built following the release of his official itinerary. On Monday, the prime minister will meet Keralam Chief Minister V. D. Satheesan and Keralam Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar to strengthen bilateral cooperation in key sectors, including trade, investment, tourism, healthcare, and education.

items.title: Family appeals for Smart team to stay, continue Nepal search
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The family of missing Malaysian hiker Muhammad Muhaimin Azhad Noor Hadi, 27, has urged the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart) to continue the search and rescue (SAR) operation in Nepal. The family said they were disappointed and frustrated after learning that the Smart team involved in the flood relief mission in Nepal was expected to return to Malaysia soon. Noor Hadi said the family and relatives were appealing for the search to continue.

items.title: Social media overtakes TV, news websites as Malaysians’ main source of news
items.summary: Television followed at 52 per cent, while news websites were used by 51 per cent. In 2017, television led at 73 per cent and news websites at 69 per cent, while social media stood at 54 per cent. Nearly seven in 10 respondents used social media for news in 2026, compared with 42 per cent for news websites and 36 per cent for television.

items.title: Sarawak police close final chapter as Long Lellang crash victims return to families
items.summary: MIRI, Sept 12 — The remains of all five victims of the Sept 8 helicopter crash in Long Lellang have been handed over to their respective families, said Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah. He said the remaining process involved identifying the victims’ personal belongings for handover to their families. He said two of the victims would be flown to Peninsular Malaysia, while the other three would be buried in Miri and Kuching.

items.title: Home Ministry to announce effective date for citizenship amendments once ready
items.summary: KULIM, Sept 12 — The Home Ministry (KDN) will announce the effective date of amendments to citizenship provisions for children born overseas to Malaysian women once all preparations for their implementation have been completed. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the preparations included the relevant documentation, citizenship regulations and an online application system, which would also involve Malaysian representative offices worldwide. He said that out of approximately 50,000 outstanding citizenship applications that previously needed to be processed, about 7,000 involved children born overseas to Malaysian mothers.

items.title: Zahid says door for Umno-PAS cooperation ‘wide open’, eyes million-strong unity rally ahead of GE16
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — The presence of PAS leaders at this year’s Umno general assembly signals the potential for Malaysia’s two largest Malay-based parties to cooperate again, Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said today. PAS secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan led a delegation of his party leaders to the Umno assembly opening yesterday. Zahid also instructed Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh to work with his counterparts in PAS and gather over a million Malay-Muslims for a mammoth rally he dubbed “Himpunan Perpaduan Ummah”.

items.title: Umno’s exit from unity govt would demand fresh mandate, not backroom deal, says Zahid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said today that the party's removal from the unity government would require a fresh mandate to determine the country's next administration. He said there would be only two options if Umno were asked to leave the government: hold a general election to obtain a fresh mandate, or formally remove the party and hold a vote of no confidence in the Dewan Rakyat. “Don't ask us to leave the government.

items.title: ‘One for you, one for me’: Tok Mat calls for PAS to put its unity talk to the test after Melaka election
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Umno should press for snap elections in one of the four states ruled by Perikatan Nasional to test the sincerity of PAS, Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said today. Mohamad, popularly known as Tok Mat, said the era of one-party rule was over, but Umno should not let other parties take advantage of its generosity in political pacts. “Ask them to hold elections in one of the SG4 states,” the Umno deputy president said, using the initials for the four state governments controlled by PAS — Kelantan, Terengganu, Kedah and Perlis.

items.title: Male elephant roaming near Terengganu village caught, now on a banana diet
items.summary: KUALA BERANG, Sept 12 — The Terengganu Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) captured a wild male elephant that was roaming in Kampung Kolam, Ajil, near here on Thursday. He said the elephant would be fed banana trunks twice a day by the department staff before being relocated to a suitable location. On Sept 10, the Hulu Terengganu Wildlife Department office received a report regarding a wild elephant roaming in Kampung Kolam.

items.title: Nurses wanted: Public Service Commission says 400 posts still open despite hiring push
items.summary: KUALA KANGSAR, Sept 12 — The Public Service Commission (SPA) has filled more than 1,000 nursing vacancies in the public service to date, with open interviews being conducted to expedite the recruitment process. Also present were Department of Orang Asli Development Director-General Muhammad Akmal Ila Ahmad, SPA Secretary Datuk Ikhbal Hanam Mukras and Kampung Orang Asli Ulu Chenein village head Din Alang. Ahmad Jailani said the open interview and walk-in methods were introduced early this year through several career carnivals organised by SPA nationwide, providing more opportunities for qualified youths to join the public service.

items.title: From speech to GE16 manifesto: BN locks in Blue Malaysia Agenda
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — The Blue Malaysia Agenda outlined by Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi will be reflected in Barisan Nasional’s (BN) manifesto for the 16th General Election (GE16), says BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir. He said the agenda formed part of the coalition’s efforts to formulate an approach that ensured Malaysia remained peaceful and stable, while navigating current and future challenges. Yesterday, Ahmad Zahid said Umno and BN would outline the Blue Malaysia Agenda to shape the nation’s trajectory heading towards the centenary of its independence, should the coalition return to lead Putrajaya.

items.title: RM60,000 versus RM500,000: Penang chief minister says still weighing DAP’s call for equal funding law
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 12 — The Penang government is unlikely to table a proposed law guaranteeing equal constituency development funds (CDF) at the coming state legislative assembly sitting, due to time constraints. Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said he had instructed the state legal adviser to prepare a draft enactment. He said the state government needed time to examine its details, adding that an engagement session with stakeholders would also be required.

items.title: Kon Yeow orders excos to clear unfinished Penang2030 projects before he steps down as chief minister
items.summary: He said the directive was issued several weeks ago, and that he was personally monitoring the outstanding initiatives. Chow said he would seek explanations from state excos overseeing portfolios that had recorded slow progress. “Penang has established 384 urban farms, but agricultural productivity remains below the state’s target,” he said during his presentation.

items.title: As new law on campus politics takes shape, minister sorts students into two camps — ‘Agree’ and ‘Disagree’
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Discussions are under way with all relevant parties on the drafting of a new law to replace the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (UUCA), said Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir. He said the new law should not only take into account current needs, but also address the challenges the country may face in the future. “I have said repeatedly that UUCA was introduced 54 years ago.

items.title: Come set up shop in KL, Anwar says to Ethiopia after decades apart
items.summary: NEW DELHI, Sept 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim extended an invitation to Ethiopia to establish an Embassy in Kuala Lumpur during his bilateral meeting with his counterpart, Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed. Malaysia’s reopening of its embassy in Addis Ababa in September 2025, after 43 years, marked significant progress in bilateral relations. Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed visited Malaysia in 2024, while Anwar visited Ethiopia in 2025.

items.title: NSE southbound lane near Menora Tunnel reopens after slope deemed safe
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 12 — The left lane of the North-South Expressway (NSE) southbound at KM263.6, which was temporarily closed following a landslide yesterday, has been reopened to all vehicles at 1pm today. “As such, the southbound left lane was reopened to all vehicles at 1pm. Earlier, the left lane at the landslide site at KM263.6 of the North-South Expressway (southbound) was closed, spanning about one kilometre.

items.title: Anwar-Modi Brics meeting: Semiconductor ties, bilateral trade take centre stage
items.summary: NEW DELHI, Sept 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his Indian counterpart Narendra Modi discussed deepening semiconductor cooperation and translating it into industry partnerships during their bilateral meeting here today. Anwar spoke about integrated supply chains, talent development and two-way investment during the meeting held on the sidelines of the 18th Brics Leaders’ Summit. Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, reaffirmed Malaysia’s commitment to increasing bilateral trade and investment, enhancing cooperation across various sectors, as well as implementing measures to facilitate and expedite Malaysian exports to India.

items.title: ‘My brother’: PM Anwar, Modi meet on Brics sidelines
items.summary: NEW DELHI, Sept 12 — “My brother” had the rare honour of becoming the warm greeting between Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his Indian counterpart Narendra Modi at their bilateral meeting here today. The two leaders met on the sidelines of the 18th Bric Leaders’ Summit at the Hyderabad House, which is the State Guest House under the Ministry of External Affairs. It is used for bilateral meetings, state banquets and meetings with foreign leaders.

items.title: A spring in Umno’s step: Three things we learnt from its 2026 general assembly
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Umno’s annual general assembly ended yesterday with a sense of optimism rarely seen at the party’s recent assemblies, as delegates filled the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur with renewed enthusiasm for the party. Umno members gather for the opening of the 2026 Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur on September 11, 2026. Umno members wave party flags during the opening of the 2026 Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur on September 11, 2026.

items.title: After Bandar Tasik Selatan PPR gets RM350,000 makeover, MP asks residents to ‘take good care’ for sake of kids and grandkids
items.summary: Bandar Tun Razak Member of Parliament Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail said repair works on the lifts at the apartments would also be carried out soon to ensure residents’ comfort. We must work together to develop and maintain them so that our children and grandchildren can also enjoy the benefits,” she said while officiating the Bandar Tun Razak Parliamentary Constituency Kenduri Rakyat Madani 2026 programme here today. Dr Wan Azizah said the initiative demonstrated how collaboration among the community, management bodies and the private sector could deliver better facilities for residents.

items.title: ‘We still have until February 2028’, Pakatan sec-gen says as GE16 chatter grows
items.summary: PEKAN, Sept 12 — Pakatan Harapan secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail today brushed aside calls for the 16th general election to be held earlier, saying the Madani government’s term only expires in February 2028. Saifuddin Nasution was responding to questions from reporters after officiating the launch of the 2026 Madani Adopted Village and School by the Immigration Department at Sekolah Kebangsaan Nenasi here, national news agency Bernama reported. Anwar is from the same party and coalition as Saifuddin Nasution.

items.title: Were the 30 Malaysians caught in Indonesia lone scammers, or something bigger? Home Ministry to dig deeper
items.summary: PEKAN, Sept 12 — Malaysia will conduct an investigation following the detention of 30 Malaysians suspected of being involved in online scam activities in Pontianak, West Kalimantan, Indonesia. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the country’s authorities would take appropriate action regarding the matter. Meanwhile, Saifuddin Nasution, who is also Pakatan Harapan secretary-general, said the Madani Government’s focus was currently on prioritising issues affecting the people.

items.title: Foreign Ministry seeks DNA samples of Nepal flood victims to identify missing Malaysians
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Malaysia is reportedly in talks with Nepal to have DNA samples from flood victims found during search-and-rescue operations sent here for matching against samples taken from relatives of Malaysians who remain missing, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said today. According to Utusan Malaysia , Mohamad said the initiative was proposed because Nepalese authorities face shortages of facilities and equipment needed to identify victims. Mohamad reportedly said Malaysia was also considering sending DNA experts to Nepal, while the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu has asked Nepalese security authorities to forward samples already collected from recovered victims.

items.title: Mission done, but not over: Smart team on way home as Nepal search continues
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — The Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart), which participated in the Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief mission in Nepal, is expected to return home today or tomorrow, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan. “The Smart team leader will provide a report and assess the next steps so that we do not make hasty decisions; if they (Nepal) require assistance from Malaysia, we can consider helping with the search or rescue operations,” he said. The Smart MAS01 team, participating in the Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief mission to Nepal, arrived in the country via Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu, on September 5.

items.title: Anwar to Iran: Keep Hormuz open, choose diplomacy over conflict
items.summary: NEW DELHI, Sept 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim expressed concern over the continued conflict and escalation across West Asia during a bilateral meeting with Iran President Masoud Pezeshkian today. “Malaysia urged all parties to return to dialogue and diplomacy to resolve disputes and de-escalate the situation,” the prime minister said during a 30-minute meeting between the two leaders on the sidelines of the summit here. Anwar, who is also finance minister, welcomed Putrajaya and Tehran’s long-standing diplomatic relations and reaffirmed cooperation on various fronts.

items.title: Umno won’t ‘betray anyone’ or seek new PM before next general election, says Asyraf Wajdi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki today said the party would not seek to change the prime minister or form a new government before the next general election is called. He said Umno remained committed to political stability and had yet to begin negotiations for the next general election. Speculation over Umno strengthening political ties with PAS intensified after PAS secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan and several other senior party leaders attended the Umno General Assembly yesterday.
